sources.label: rent roll: 64 of 70 units let at 2026-09-30

discrepancies.why: The rent roll is unit-level and dated 2026-09-30; the OM figure (as of June 2026) is a headline the screen cannot trace to units. A gap of 6.6 points is about 5 units.

impact.basis: 5 units x average in-place rent AED 107,367: income the OM implies but the roll does not show (estimate)

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for the Ejari export and the vacancy list at the rent-roll date; reconcile the OM figure to unit numbers.

sources.quote: Tenure Title deed in the name of the Seller (land and building)
sources.label: OM title

sources.quote: Title deed in the name of the Seller (land and building)
sources.label: verified quote

sources.quote: Transfer is subject to the purchaser meeting Dubai Land Department ownership eligibility for the plot.
sources.label: verified quote

sources.quote: Al Barsha 1 is an established, largely owner-built district of mid-rise residential buildings and villas
sources.label: verified quote

discrepancies.why: The mandate requires freehold single title; the OM states tenure unstated, ownership single_title. The screen does not decide title; until legal confirms it, nothing else about the deal matters. Review: The OM says whose name the title deed is in but never says freehold. The Terms of Sale make transfer conditional on the purchaser meeting DLD ownership eligibility for the plot, and the OM tells purchasers to take their own advice. That wording suggests the plot may be non-freehold or restricted by nationality. The 'owner-built' district description points the same way. If the plot is restricted, an institutional buyer may be unable to buy it, which would change whether the deal fits the mandate.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Obtain the title deed(s) and DLD ownership records; legal to confirm freehold status and any nationality restriction before any further work.

discrepancies.title: Unit-mix average rents multiply out to more than the stated contracted rent
discrepancies.why: Average rent times unit count gives about AED 7.41m across all 70 units (24×77,675 + 30×111,500 + 12×136,583 + 4×139,250). That is about AED 0.53m above the AED 6,871,500 'contracted' figure. The OM does not say whether the averages cover let units only or all units. If they include vacant units at asking rent, the unit-mix table mixes potential rent with in-place rent.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Reconcile the unit-mix averages to the rent roll, let units only against all units. Confirm that AED 6,871,500 is in-place contracted rent from let units only, with vacant units excluded.

discrepancies.title: Headline net yield and NOI are before any vacancy or collection allowance

sources.quote: Figures before vacancy and collection allowances.
sources.label: verified quote

sources.quote: Net yield on total acquisition cost 5.88%
sources.label: verified quote

discrepancies.why: The 5.88% 'net' yield is built on contracted rent and other income with no vacancy or collection loss deducted. The income statement shows no such lines either, and it is unaudited and on a cash basis. The OM's 98% occupancy figure also conflicts with the rent roll. The real net yield is therefore likely lower than the 5.88% headline.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Request the audited or bank-reconciled statements and the 12-month collections ledger. Re-underwrite NOI using the rent roll's actual occupancy and a vacancy and collection allowance.

notices.text: The rent roll is dated 30 September 2026, 52 days before the screen date. Ask for a current roll before relying on occupancy and expiries.
Tenants' security deposits of AED 361,975 transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
Cheque profile: 36% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 40% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 24% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
Building condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age (MEP, lifts, facade, waterproofing).
Retail leases: permitted use, trade licences and VAT treatment of shop rents.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Decline**: Al Barsha 1 is outside the mandate's permitted areas, which is a hard filter, so the deal fails on location before anything else is considered.

Title is also unresolved. The OM does not state tenure, and nothing else matters until legal confirms the buyer can own the plot. I give no walk-away price and no buy recommendation.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Al Mehrab Building in Al Barsha 1. It has 70 units [[om.unit_count]] and was completed in 2009 [[deal.completion_year]].
- **Price:** The ask is AED 76.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. The OM quotes AED 898 per sq ft [[om.price_psf_stated]] on net sellable area.
- **Income:** The rent roll shows in-place rent of AED 6.9m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]] on direct leases, with no master tenant. 64 units [[rr.let_units]] are let and 6 [[rr.vacant_units]] are vacant, which is 91% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupancy by units. The OM states 98% [[om.occupancy_stated]].

## Returns
For reference only; not decisive. The deal was not underwritten because it fails the mandate filters, so there are no IRR, multiple, yield or DSCR figures. The OM's headline yield is 5.9% [[om.yield_stated]], stated as net on total cost. We have not rebuilt it on the buyer's basis. It deducts no vacancy or collection loss.

## What would make it fail
It already fails on location. If the mandate were ever widened, the title and eligibility question would come first. After that, the OM's occupancy and yield are overstated against the rent roll, so real income is lower than the OM implies.

## Discrepancies
Lower-severity items are not discussed.

1. **Title (high).** The OM says whose name the deed is in but never says freehold. The sale terms make transfer conditional on the purchaser meeting DLD ownership eligibility for the plot. That suggests the plot may be non-freehold or restricted by nationality, and an institutional buyer might be unable to buy. The screen relied on nothing here; legal must confirm.
2. **Occupancy and headline yield (high and medium; one gap, impact counted once).**
   - The OM says 98% [[om.occupancy_stated]] as of June 2026 [[om.occupancy_as_of]]. The rent roll dated 30 September 2026 [[rr.as_of]] shows 91% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]]. The screen relied on the rent roll because it is unit-level.
   - The gap is 6.6 points [[disc.occupancy_mismatch.why]], about 5 units [[disc.occupancy_mismatch.why]]. That is roughly AED 537k [[disc.occupancy_mismatch.impact_aed]] of income the OM implies and the roll does not show.
   - The OM's 5.88% [[disc.other_om_claim.why]] net yield deducts no vacancy or collection loss. The income statement is unaudited and on a cash basis, so the real net yield is likely lower.

## Checks before diligence
- Blocking: get the title deed and DLD ownership records. Legal must confirm freehold status and any nationality restriction before any further work.
- Get the Ejari export and the vacancy list at the rent-roll date, and reconcile the OM occupancy to unit numbers.
- Request audited or bank-reconciled statements and the 12-month collections ledger. Re-underwrite NOI at actual occupancy with a vacancy and collection allowance.
- The rent roll is 52 days [[notice.stale_rent_roll]] old. Ask for a current roll before relying on occupancy and expiries.
- Security deposits of AED 362k [[rr.deposits_aed]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Review the cheque profile. More cheques per lease mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.
- Standard first-pass items:
  - Completion certificate for the as-built building.
  - Affection plan and permitted use.
  - Civil Defence and fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
  - Condition survey and capex plan for a building of this age.
  - Retail leases: permitted use, trade licences and VAT treatment.

## Assumptions
No house-view assumptions were applied, because the deal was not underwritten. The soft mandate tests (yield, IRR, multiple, occupancy, expiry concentration and over-renting) are unknown and would count as soft misses. They are not decisive here.
